architecture.title: The multi-agent chatbot on one Spark — a supervisor LLM, four MCP tools, specialists on the Docker network
architecture.caption: From the playbook's docker-compose.yml, docker-compose-models.yml and backend/client.py. Only the frontend (:3000), backend (:8000), Postgres (:5432) and Milvus (:19530, :9091) publish host ports; the model servers are reached by container name on chatbot-net (http://<name>:8000/v1). The supervisor is forbidden to write code or answer from documents itself, and the tool loop stops after 3 iterations.

sequence.title: A dependent request: 'search my documents, then build a website from them'
sequence.caption: The supervisor prompt's own few-shot example: a call whose arguments depend on another call's output is staged, not batched. Lab 19-3 does the retrieval step with stdlib TF-IDF instead of Qwen3 vectors in Milvus; exercise 19 builds the graph context txt2kg would add.

steps.label: search my documents for design requirements, then build a website
final answer built on both tool results

charts.title: Lab 19-3 — stdlib TF-IDF over 65 playbook READMEs, 8 questions with known answers
charts.caption: Measured on this Mac (retrieval is arithmetic, identical on every machine; dgx-spark-playbooks@3410c65, 1510 sections). Both misses at #1 lost to playbooks sharing the words, not the intent (VLM, VS Code).

charts.title: Lab 19-2 — txt2kg's prompt on three playbook paragraphs: facts vs. a connected graph
charts.caption: LAPTOP STAND-IN, measured in one run on this Mac (extraction is sampled; a second run gave the same pattern). Good-looking triples, a fragmented graph: the only cross-document entity was the word 'playbook'. Entity resolution, not extraction, is the hard part.
